questions.q: What did Munger do during the Second World War?
a: He served as a pilot in the army
He worked in military intelligence
He studied engineering at Harvard
He ran a small law practice
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he trained as a pilot and joined the army, then later finished Harvard Law with honors.

questions.q: What habit did Munger insist on in his work?
a: Getting things right the first time
Reviewing every decision twice
Delegating the hardest tasks
Working faster than competitors
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he insisted on finishing things the first time rather than going back to repeat the process.

questions.q: What did Berkshire Hathaway's success rest on, according to the summary?
a: A strong work ethic and moral principles
Aggressive deal-making and secrecy
Hiring the most expensive analysts
Acting on inside information quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the firm was built on hard work and, more importantly, a set of moral principles.

questions.q: How did Munger respond when a middleman confessed a costly mistake?
a: He forgave him and let him keep his job
He fired him on the spot
He sued him for the losses
He moved him to a junior role
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the man owned up immediately, and that honesty was why Munger forgave him.

questions.q: What does Munger's See's Candy story illustrate?
a: Being willing to change your mind when others make a case
Trusting your first instinct over other opinions
Avoiding investments in food businesses
Never admitting a bad call in public
questions.why: Lesson 3 says others changed his mind about See's Candy and urges readers to take second looks at decisions.
